intelligence.human_view: A contract is a document people sign without reading, and the reason is not laziness — it is that contracts are built to be unreadable: walls of text, words that need a dictionary, no way in. The unfold inverts the whole shape. One block at a time, each one opening only when the reader asks it to, each one taking its own color as it opens so progress is visible, jewel bullets and explanations doing the work that fine print never could. And it is never forced — the reader can agree without reading, or unfold everything at once — because a forced reading is not a reading, it is a hostage situation, and a signature extracted that way is worth nothing. The eyes are the second inversion: instead of pretending there are no hard words, the agreement marks every one of them — Smart Link, clearing hold, ambassador, points — and explains it in plain words, in place, the moment the reader could stall. The rule is the test: if a cold reader could stall on it, it gets an eye. And the last line is the discipline that holds the whole thing together: professional comes from presentation and explanations, not from bigger words. A child and a grandma still follow every line — or the agreement isn't finished.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a beautiful treasure book! You read the first page, then you tap it — and the next page unfolds like magic! Down and down, page by page, until the very end! And if there's a tricky word, there's a little eye you can tap, and it explains it in easy words! You never HAVE to read it all — but it's so beautiful, you'll want to!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like a proper official letter that opens itself, love — one lovely page at a time, each one its own colour, all beautifully presented. And if there's a word you don't know, there's a little eye beside it that explains it in plain words, right there. Nobody forces you to read it all — but it's so clear and so beautiful, you'll want to. That's how a real agreement should feel.
intelligence.naya_view: I unfold the agreement block by block — read, click, read — down and down to the Agree button, each block taking its own new spectrum color as it opens, all elevated, jewel bullets, explanations. Never forced: agree without reading, or unfold it all at once. The eye at the top-right says in a nutshell what it is and why it matters, in his words. Every hard word gets a little eye beside it — if a cold reader could stall on it, it gets an eye. Professional comes from presentation and explanations, not bigger words — child and grandma still follow every line.
